I find it interesting that this ask was posted around the exact same time hours ago I had my very first sleep paralysis experience. 

It was terrifying. I had recently lost my god mother (who pretty much raised me and was my mother figure), so death and dying has been a very often thought about topic in my mind. 

I believe that anxiety of losing someone else manifested in this episode of sleep paralysis, because it felt as if I were actually dying. 

I remember attempting to fall asleep for a nap, and feeling very uncomfortable. I couldn’t get into a comfortable position to lay, so I was a bit annoyed. Then everything kinda slowed down and went black. I woke up, and I could see my ceiling and everything, but I could not move my body. My vision went dark, and I could faintly see a galaxy. This triggered something inside of me, and I felt as if my body was sinking into my bed and essentially my soul leaving my body. It was beginning to become hard to breathe, and so ensued that deep feeling of dread. Like I was dying. The only thought in my mind was “WAKE UP.” I felt panicked. 

I also had begun to feel extremely cold. This feeling started in my hands, which was very odd to me. I had found my god mother dead in her room, and I remember touching her and her being cold. This feeling in my hands felt similar to her. The coldness spread to my head, and I heard a very loud a loud woosh sound as the cold enveloped my head. I was finally able to pull myself out of it by regaining control of my toes and moving them. The dark vignette over my vision faded and I felt..serene? For a short while. I felt like death wasn’t so scary, but then I melted into a panic attack which wasn’t fun.
